ImageDescription.value: Robert Cavelier de LaSalle Monument, Lincoln Park, Chicago, Illinois. Artist: Count Jacques de la Laing (1858–1917) . It was cast in Belgium and shipped to Chicago in three parts. The monument was unveiled West Stockton Drive in Lincoln on October 12, 1889, but became a traffic impediment. It was moved to North Clark Street in the mid-1920s, and to its present location in the 1990s.

originalCandidate.title: File:Ulysses S. Grant Monument, Lincoln Park, Lake Shore Drive, Lincoln Park, Chicago, IL (54516501247).jpg

ObjectName.value: Ulysses S. Grant Monument, Lincoln Park, Lake Shore Drive, Lincoln Park, Chicago, IL (54516501247)

Categories.value: Lincoln Park (Chicago)|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|Photographs by Warren LeMay in Chicago

ImageDescription.value: Built in 1885-1891, this Richardsonian Romanesque Revival-style monument was designed by Louis Rebisso to honor United States Army General and former United States President Ulysses S. Grant (1822-1885).  The monument features a rough-hewn gray granite base with roman arched openings, which once carried a carriage path across a berm while allowing for unimpeded travel beneath, a gray rough-hewn granite pavilion with roman arched openings, and a bronze statue of Grant on horseback atop the roof of the pavilion.  The monument is one of several in Lincoln Park, and is characteristic of large-scale late 19th Century monument design, which often incorporated some form of functionality into their design.

Credit.value: Ulysses S. Grant Monument, Lincoln Park, Lake Shore Drive, Lincoln Park, Chicago, IL

Artist.value: Warren LeMay from Chicago, IL, United States
